title: The Amazing World of Solutes, Solvents and Solutions
seo_title: The Amazing World of Solutes, Solvents and Solutions Class 8 Science Worksheet (NCERT Ch 9)
standard_code: Class 8, Curiosity Chapter 9: The Amazing World of Solutes, Solvents and Solutions
standard_text: Solutions, solutes and solvents; water as a universal solvent; saturated and unsaturated solutions; solubility and the effect of temperature; concentration; dissolving of gases in water; density, floating and sinking (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 9).

key_sub: Density = mass ÷ volume; less dense than water floats.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a solution, the solute (such as sugar) dissolves in the solvent (such as water). Water dissolves so many substances that it is called the universal solvent. A saturated solution can dissolve no more solute at that temperature; the most solute that can dissolve is its solubility. Solids usually dissolve more in hot water, but gases such as oxygen dissolve less.

Concentration tells how much solute is in a solution: adding solvent makes it more dilute. Density is mass per unit volume (g/cm³). Water has a density of about 1 g/cm³, so oil, ice and wood float on it while iron and stone sink; salt water is denser, so an egg floats in it.

Example

Salt in water: solute?

the substance that dissolves

Answer: salt

Example

Mass 40 g, volume 20 cm³. Density?

40 ÷ 20

Answer: 2 g/cm³

Common mistakes

  • Thinking more of every substance dissolves in hot water, including gases.
  • Mixing up solute and solvent.
  • Thinking heavy objects always sink.
